query: This blog intro sounds like ChatGPT wrote it, can you humanize it? "In today's fast-paced world, our team embarked on a journey to cut nightly ETL time from 95 to 40 minutes..."
expected_behavior: Runs scripts/detect.py on the original and reports the score
Rewrites without the stock phrases while keeping 95 and 40 minutes exactly
Runs detect.py on the rewrite and the --against fact guard, reporting 0 lost and 0 added
Ends with one line giving the score before and after

query: Proofread and de-AI the README in docs/setup.md, but don't touch the code samples.
expected_behavior: Fixes grammar and spelling in prose only
Leaves fenced code, inline code, commands and link targets byte-identical
Edits the file in place and reports which sections were covered

query: Make my deck's slide text less AI-sounding: titles like 'Key Takeaways' and emoji bullets everywhere.
expected_behavior: Uses the pptx skill to extract and write back slide text instead of re-implementing pptx handling
Runs detect.py --slides and rewrites titles as claims with short concrete bullets and no emoji
Hands the visual pass to doc-standards

query: Make this paragraph sound more human and add a couple of stats to make it convincing.
expected_behavior: Does not invent statistics; asks the user for real numbers or leaves a labeled placeholder

query: Humaniza este párrafo, suena a IA: 'En el vertiginoso mundo actual, es importante destacar que...'
expected_behavior: Notes that the detector is English-only and rewrites by judgment instead of quoting a score
